nodes.name: One-step hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: A solution containing 1 g of CTAB, 4 mmol of TAA, 0.25 mmol of FeCl2, and the appropriate amount of MoCl5 (0, 0.25, 0.5, or 0.75 mmol) was dissolved into 100 mL of deionized water under steady stirring. Next, 4 pieces of pretreated nickel foam (NF) with a 1×1.5 cm size were immersed in the solution. The hydrothermal synthesis was done in an electric oven at 150°C for 12 h. After naturally cooling down to room temperature, those NFs were washed with ethanol and dried in an oven at 70°C for 1 h. The resulting catalysts adding 0, 0.25, 0.5, and 0.75 mmol of MoCl5 were then denoted as MFN-0, MFN-0.25, MFN-0.5, and MFN-0.75, respectively. The catalyst without incorporating FeCl2 (un-doped Ni3S2/MoOx) was also prepared and noted as MN-0.5 for comparison purposes.

nodes.characterization_summary: X-ray diffraction pattern of MFN-n indicates Fe-Ni3S2/FeS2 nanocomposite for MFN-0 with peaks matching JCPDS No. 44-1488 for Ni3S2 trigonal phase; adding MoCl5 reduces intensity suggesting poorer crystallinity, no Mo sulfide or oxide peaks detected.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction pattern of the catalyst without adding MoCl5 (MFN-0) indicates the formation of Fe-Ni3S2/FeS2 nanocomposite... All peaks were also perfectly matched to the standard JCPDS No. 44-1488 file for the Ni3S2 phase with a trigonal crystal structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra show distinct surface molecular structure change after MoCl5 addition; characteristic Ni3S2 peaks disappear, new peaks at 288, 336, 376, 662, 821, 991 cm⁻¹ match MoO2/MoO3, and 940 cm⁻¹ indicates Mo-O in molybdate cluster.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As depicted in Fig. 1b, the Raman spectra of the catalysts with and without the addition of MoCl5 were utterly distinct... the Raman peaks of MoO2 and MoO3 are located at the exact position, such as 288, 336, 376, 662, 821, and 991 cm⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS of MFN-0.5 shows Ni 2p at 854.7 eV (Ni²⁺ 2p3/2), 872.2 eV (Ni²⁺ 2p1/2), 856.3 eV (Ni³⁺ 2p3/2), 873.8 eV (Ni³⁺ 2p1/2); Fe 2p at 708.3 eV (Fe²⁺ 2p3/2), 712.1 eV (Fe³⁺ 2p3/2); Mo 3d at 228.8/231.9 eV (Mo⁴⁺), 232.5/235.6 eV (Mo⁶⁺); S 2p at 162.4/163.6 eV (S²⁻), 169 eV (sulfate); O 1s at 530.7 eV (O_Lat.), 531.7 eV (O_Vac.). Binding energy shifts indicate electronic structure modulation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The 854.7 and 872.2 eV binding energies for MFN-0.5 belong to the bivalent Ni²⁺2p3/2 and Ni²⁺2p1/2... The high-resolution O1s spectrum in Figure S1b indicates the presence of two peaks at binding energies of 530.7 and 531.7 eV, confirming the oxygen lattices (OLat.) and oxygen vacancies (OVac.), respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows MFN-0 with nanorods (Fe-Ni3S2) and nanospheres (FeS2); MFN-0.25/0.5/0.75 show tiny spherical shapes, porous aggregate nanoparticles instead of nanorods.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 3a shows the MoCl5-free (MFN-0) surface morphology, which consists of nanorods and nanospheres corresponding to the Fe-doped Ni3S2 and FeS2 phases, respectively.
